title: A primary intraosseous cystic meningioma: Case report
journal: International Journal of Surgery Case Reports
case_prompt:
A 62-year-old man presented with a two-year history of a slowly enlarging swelling of the lateral wall of his left orbit. The mass had a hard consistency, was slightly painful on palpation, and was associated with mild left proptosis. 

Magnetic resonance imaging showed a large intradiploic lesion involving the lateral orbital wall and greater wing of the sphenoid. On T2-weighted sequences, the lesion was hyperintense, with a non-homogeneous, relatively hypointense round component. On FLAIR sequences the lesion was hypointense. After intravenous contrast, the round component demonstrated a mildly non-homogeneous increase in signal intensity.

Computed tomography of the skull revealed a 23 × 32 mm osteolytic lesion in the same region. Most of the lesion appeared fluid-filled, while a solid portion measuring 8 × 9 mm displayed heterogeneous contrast enhancement.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Considered meningoencephalocele — “meningoencefalocele presents as a combination of fluid-filled cyst and parenchyma, which, unlike tumor tissue, isn’t enhanced by the contrast agent; moreover in three-dimensional MRI reconstructions it is possible to note continuity between intracranial brain parenchyma and herniated parenchyma.”  
2. Considered intradiploic arachnoid cyst — “in the case of an arachnoid cyst there are no mural nodules.”  
3. Considered intradiploic dermoid or epidermoid tumor — “the differential diagnosis between the lesion we operated on and a dermoid or epidermoid tumor … is mainly ascribable to the difference of intensity of signal in the MRI and of density in a CT scan between the cholesterol or fat and the liquor-like fluid of the tumor cyst.”  
4. Considered intraosseous lipoma — “the differential diagnosis … of a lipoma is mainly ascribable to the difference of intensity of signal in the MRI and of density in a CT scan between the cholesterol or fat and the liquor-like fluid of the tumor cyst.”  
5. Favored meningioma based on the presence of an intradiploic cystic lesion with an enhancing mural nodule within a skull bone.
